scope: Unified virtual cursor, readable result headings, configurable Google-default search and main-menu labels.

topics.title: Default search engine
details: Google is the initial default for typed searches, Search the web requests and follow-up searches. Options, Web browser includes Default search engine. Google, Bing, Brave Search and DuckDuckGo are retained choices; the installed browser selection remains separate.

Say Default search engine Google, Set default search engine Brave Search, or Search engine DuckDuckGo. Explicit engine-name searches use that engine for the request. The selected search engine is not silently replaced after unreadable results or human verification. The setting is saved with the other preferences.

topics.title: Word processor and Notepad
details: Documents on the main menu is now Word processor, with W as its first-letter key. Notes is now Notepad, with N. Say Word processor, Open word processor, Notepad or Open Notepad to open them. Existing document and note commands, file locations and editing functions remain available.

topics.title: One virtual cursor for page navigation
details: Quick element navigation, link/heading lists, keyboard reading and voice reading use the same virtual page position. After H, Shift+H, K, Tab or other element navigation, subsequent arrow reading continues from the selected element. The reading editor receives a cursor revision independently of outstanding caret acknowledgments. Stale read-only caret events are discarded rather than moving the cursor back.

Left/Right reads characters, Ctrl+Left/Right moves words, Up/Down reads lines while preserving the preferred column, Ctrl+Up/Down moves paragraphs, Home/End moves within the line and Page Up/Page Down makes longer jumps. Ctrl+Home/End reaches the page boundaries. Shift selection and Ctrl+C remain available in the read-only view; a new element jump clears the selection. Editable fields keep their ordinary typing/caret behavior.

Incidental DOM changes remap the selected element by its stable key when preceding text shifts. Active read-only selections are protected from background buffer replacement. Continue reading retains its continuation rather than restarting. Existing automatic field/choice handling and form review safeguards remain in place.

topics.title: Result headings and link activation
details: Readable heading title text takes precedence over URL/breadcrumb metadata, including URL-only ARIA labels. URL-only metadata headings are excluded from heading destinations when no readable title is available. Heading and link positions point at their title text in the virtual buffer.

The original DOM identity is retained for validating link activation. Enter on a heading contained in a link opens that associated link; Enter in the separate headings list continues to move to the heading without opening it.

topics.title: Documentation and verification
details: Built-in Help and every versioned What’s New format document the new menu labels, retained engines, default setting and virtual-reading behavior. Regression tests cover stale caret events, selection, search routing, voice/keyboard interchange and reading continuation.

Live browser fixtures cover result title metadata, headings/links, arrows after jumps, DOM reflow and safe activation. Windows integration checks actual editor caret positions and keyboard navigation across Firefox, Chrome, Edge and Brave. These checks do not replace beta testing on individual public websites.
